notes.note: Not a compile-time rule; tested positively: after a receive with a template variable containing '?', the template is still not a value (isvalue false) and matches a different second message.
Titan accepts: it does not enforce complete initialization of templates statically (unbound fields are only detected at runtime). Rejection follows from 15.1 b) together with 15.3 d).

Tested negatively: a fourth value-list element intended as return value in a signature template is rejected; the positive side (return value given via value clause of reply/getreply) is covered by 15.02_test_003.

Reading 2 chosen: call template defines in/inout values, reply template defines out/inout values. Redirects use assignment notation because Titan rejects the full-length list notation with '-' for out parameters that the standard's own examples use.

Titan accepts: it does not check the specific-value restriction on call templates at compile time (only at runtime). The template is a global non-parameterized template, so the violation is statically detectable.
Titan accepts: no static check of in/inout parameters of call templates (indirect matching mechanism via referenced template).

Reading 1 chosen (call operation). That the out-parameter value of the call template is not transmitted cannot be observed directly; the test checks that a call with Par2 := 99 is accepted by a getcall with Par2 := - and delivers the correct in/inout values.
Titan accepts: no static check of value-list matching in in parameters of in-line call templates.

Tested with reply only; raise carries an exception value, not a signature parameter template. Titan accepts: no static check of out/inout parameters in reply templates, although 22.3.3 c) forbids matching mechanisms there.
Titan accepts: no static check of indirect matching mechanisms in reply templates.
Titan accepts: it does not enforce complete initialization of signature template parameter fields statically.
Titan rejects: it does not support the @deterministic template modifier (and parameterized local templates), both valid per the V4.17.1 syntax.
Templates are also permitted in component types (ComponentElementDef), so the violation places a template inside a port type body, which is neither the module definitions part nor a local scope.
Tested positively: local templates declared in a testcase, function, altstep and statement block are usable.
Titan rejects: 'Parameterized local template not supported' is a Titan limitation; the standard explicitly allows parameterized local templates.
Titan accepts: it does not enforce complete initialization of template fields not affected by parameterization.
Tested as dot notation on a template used as a redirect target (retrieving a received value into a template field).
Reading 1 chosen: '->' value redirect retrieves the received value.
Covers one restriction of 16.1.4 b) only (a send in a function called from a receiving template). Titan accepts: it does not implement 16.1.4 checks.
Titan accepts: it does not enforce complete initialization of local message templates statically.
Titan accepts: it does not check the e) conditions for signature templates.
Reading 1 chosen: a template with NotUsedSymbol out parameter used in reply. Titan accepts: no static check.
